title: Alpha↔Omega Dynamics (AΩD)
description:

Comprehension, cooperation, and presence are not prerequisites of AFC.

Nuff said.

What AΩD is

Alpha↔Omega Dynamics (AΩD) is a relational, temporal computational calculus built from the discrete Stokes cut of the Axiomatic Fundamentalism Calculus (AFC). The Stokes identity supplies boundary accounting; declared update rules let a finite model execute temporal wave dynamics.

Run finite models by hand or script: declare the support and update law, follow committed traversals, certify returns, and calculate boundary balances. Native event counts are integers, and the response examples use exact rational values. Tables record evaluated values and their provenance; tables are not the calculus.

  • main.pdf — The calculus: Ontology, certified closure, recurrence, relational time, motif folding, proofs and explicitly scoped mathematical models.
  • manual.pdf — Working with the calculus: The Declared Edge Computation (D.E.C.) ledger, calculation spine, executable fixtures, worked calculations, computational intelligence models and measured-sector comparison records.

Waves, relational time and Fourier

A certified retained-start return contributes one closure-phase cycle. At least two committed phase-bearing traversals are required, together with the bound hinge, lineage and return witness. One initial certified closure followed by at least one distinct compatible reclosure of the same retained lineage admits a recurring wave.

Relational time compares at least two coupled recurrent lineages through repeated bound contacts, yielding cadence ratios, lag and duration. Finite Fourier transforms decompose and reconstruct committed value traces of already admitted recurrence on a declared finite abelian index group. This supplies a representation for harmonic analysis, convolution and correlation after recurrence has been certified. The Fourier representation uses exact complex characters.

The engine: how to run it (raw AFC and the D.E.C. ledger)

AFC runs raw to produce trace rows, and AΩD detectors read the trace to classify motifs. The Manual exposes each arithmetic step through the Declared Edge Computation (D.E.C.) ledger, where each row records B, v, e, ve, σ(e), adm(e;B), w(e;B), P(e;B), route(e;B). Each example declares its admissible channels and weights.

  1. Branching and normalization. At a Q4 node v=(0,0,0,0), take four Hamming-1 edge slots {e1,e2,e3,e4} and ternary states σ(ei) ∈ {−1,0,+1}. Isotropic branching gives Piso=1/4. Declared anisotropic integer weights w=(1,1,4,2) with Z=8 give Pani=(1/8,1/8,1/2,1/4) across outgoing, returned and hinge routes.
  2. Blocking and hinge slide. Zero admissibility gives adm(e;B)=0 ⇒ P(e;B)=0. Blocking the additional same-resolution dwell (e3,0) removes that dwell row while retaining the structural hinge; the edge slot e3 may re-enter as an admitted branch state. For the declared slide pool {(e1,−1),(e2,−1),(e3,+1)}, separately specified weights w′=(3,3,1) with Z′=7 give Pslide=(3/7,3/7,1/7): returned weight 6/7 and outgoing weight 1/7.

The setup (The Art of the Leprechaun): how to get specific results

Tracing a cut closely enough to set up a larger relational system as a finite scale—with explicit boundary, window and accounting choices—is The Art of the Leprechaun. The Manual organizes these boundary calculations around one calculation spine:

  1. Declare the scope and boundary window. Fix a ⊢ (F, R, ∂T R, ω) and B=(∂T F,ω). A certified enclosing return supplies retained cycle provenance Cf[Σ]A↔Ω. Evaluate branch/hinge/branch AOμ(C)=⟨Πα,Hμ,ΠΩ⟩, with reflection duration RD=|Πα|+Hμ+|ΠΩ|. For equal branch support counts |Πα|=|ΠΩ|=Π, this reduces to RD=2Π+Hμ.
  2. Clip to the window and compute pressure. With neutral reflection and a compatible native-count window, duration participation clips to ρωD=min(RD,|ω|) without clipping RD or RCD. In the declared channel example, duonic pressure is pD=C3ρωD. For the outgoing tunnel branch stunnel=(e3,+1) with Ptunnel=1/7, RD=5, |ω|=2 and capacity C3=3, this gives ρωD=2, pressure pD=3×2=6, and outgoing weighted pressure contribution TtunnelD=(1/7)×6=6/7.
  3. Promote D.E.C. rows to ADAR, SADAR and boundary flux. A routed D.E.C. returned-current pair promotes to an oriented ADAR component and a boundary SADAR value 𝔖B(C)=pDC,A↔ΩAC,A↔Ω, which sums over the boundary as ΦD∂T R=∑e∈∂T R𝔖B(Ce). A separate declared example with ρωD=4, C3=3 and attention A12=1/3 gives pressure pD=12 and signed boundary value 𝔖B=pDA12=4 (or −4 for the reversed orientation of that channel). For moving boundaries, ΦD∂R,mov(t)=ΦDcross(t)−ΦDsweep(t)+ΦDshedding(t) (e.g., 8−3+2=7).
  4. Audit closure residuals, shedding and rational response. Comparing window pressure PD against a declared closure record Cclose gives signed closure residual Δclose=PD−Cclose and positive sheddic surplus Xshedding=max(0,Δclose) (for 1:2:9yro, PD=27 and Cclose=24 give Δclose=3 and Xshedding=3). For downstream state continuation, one declared response realization uses positive pressure p>0, gain g, available source set Dk and perturbation qk to advance the current by Jk+1=Jk+(Ak+qk+g∑e:ie∈Dkre)/p.

The boundary setup selects the application scope; declared support, admissibility and update laws specify the run:

  • Computational intelligence and persistent learning. Test whether a retained relation is causally operative by structurally removing it and comparing strictly later projected outcomes under matched state, response law and future inputs. Execute proprioceptive action-return models with ra=y−u on a common count projection of an issued action and its certified bound return; test learning through later causal use across zero-stimulus windows, polycadence, and feedback qk=−Jk under the declared stability conditions.
  • Exact discrete simulations. Execute double-slit cross-return fixtures Tk×=Tk0+Ck×, short-window shedding audits Xshedding=max(0,PD−Cclose), and 3D integer-lattice phase-cycle fixtures zi∈ℤ3 → Δzi(n) → Qi(n) → Qi(n) mod βa → octants → δ3. Audit bins with signed integer residuals δ3=(sgn(Δℤ),|Δℤ|).
  • Measured-sector comparisons and benchmark plans. Freeze internal outputs before comparison through declared observable maps and external units. The Manual covers rest-energy and hydrogen-series records, boundary-current examples, solar observable-map records, the SPARC five-galaxy radial diagnostic, and staged SWELLS lensing work. Each record states its support, inputs and execution status: solar native input certificates and map definitions remain unsupplied; the originating tau calculation recipe is not supplied; higher-resolution field-dynamics and L3 lensing execution depend on their stated input gates.
